standard_prerequisites.name: Reconstruction of a torsion sheaf from its pushforwards to the approximants
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the lemma stating that a torsion sheaf on the limit is the limit of the pullbacks of its pushforwards along the projections
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the expression F = lim f_i^{-1}f_{i,*}F.

standard_prerequisites.name: Cohomology of a directed limit as a colimit
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the colimit theorem computing the cohomology of the limit as the colimit of the cohomologies of the approximants
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies the identity H^q(X, F) = colim H^q(X_i, f_{i,*}F).

core_obligations: Decompose the sheaf (proof lines 19640-19644): for a torsion sheaf F on X, the reconstruction lemma gives F = lim f_i^{-1}f_{i,*}F for the projections f_i : X -> X_i.

Compute the cohomology (proof lines 19645-19648): the colimit theorem then writes H^q_etale(X, F) as the colimit of the groups H^q_etale(X_i, f_{i,*}F), each of which vanishes above the maximum of the cd(X_i); hence cd(X) is at most that maximum.
proof_roadmap: Write the torsion sheaf as the limit of the pullbacks of its pushforwards.
Apply the colimit theorem to express the cohomology on X as a colimit and read off the bound.
difficulty_reason: The lemma bounds the cohomological dimension of a directed limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes by the maximum of the dimensions of the approximants (statement lines 19632-19637). The proof (proof lines 19639-19648) expresses a torsion sheaf on the limit as the limit of the pullbacks of its pushforwards and applies the colimit theorem to compute the cohomology as a colimit, giving the bound. H2: two standard inputs, written out.
